transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?

Oh, thank you so much for taking the time to see me, Doctor. I really appreciate it. I... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably just a silly thing, but I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit at my age, but my kitchen table is just... well, it's covered. It's got my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I sit down to sort it out, and I just sit there, not knowing which thing to do first. And then somehow the whole day is just gone. I try my best, I really do, but... is that the sort of thing I should be telling you? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you struggled with organization and getting things done throughout your life, or is this something new for you?

Oh, that's a very good question, Doctor. I... well, I hope it's alright to say, but no, it's not exactly new. I hate to admit it, because I really have always tried to be good and do what's expected of me, but... I suppose I've always been a bit scatterbrained. 

Even when I was just a little girl, my teachers—they were wonderful, really—but they always wrote on my report cards that I was bright, but... well, careless. I was always forgetting my books or leaving my homework behind. And they constantly had to give me little reminders to just finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside to play. I always meant to do it right the first time, I promise. 

I feel a bit silly bringing up things from sixty years ago, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of history you're looking for?
Growing up or even now, have you often felt restless, fidgety, or had difficulty sitting still for very long?

Oh, goodness. Well... I suppose I do have a bit of, oh, nervous energy, maybe? I really try my best to be polite and sit perfectly still, I promise I do, but... well, it is a little embarrassing to admit. 

Even when I’m trying so hard to just sit quietly in a meeting—like at the church or the senior center—I... I catch myself rubbing my hands together. Or tapping my foot. Sometimes I'll be clicking my pen without even realizing I'm doing it, or just shifting around in my chair. It's dreadful, really, because I end up moving around so much that people actually look over at me. I always try to stop right away and smile, because I certainly don't want to be a bother or a disruption to anyone else. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly rude... is that the sort of restlessness you were asking about, Doctor?
Do you often find yourself speaking out of turn or interrupting others before they have finished talking?

Oh, my. Well... I certainly hope I don't do that. I was always taught that it's very impolite to interrupt when someone else has the floor. I try very, very hard to be a good listener. 

I suppose... well, sometimes I might get a little excited about a topic, or I might be worried I'll forget what I wanted to say if I don't say it right then, but... I don't think I make a habit of talking over people. At least, I really hope I don't. My husband has never scolded me for it, and the ladies at the church haven't said anything. 

I always try to wait my turn, Doctor. I really wouldn't want anyone to think I was being rude or disrespectful to them. Do you... do you think I've been interrupting you today? I'm so sorry if I have been.
Do you often feel like you are constantly 'on the go,' as if you are driven by an internal motor?

Oh, goodness, no. I... well, I don't think so, anyway. Being seventy, I'm afraid I don't have quite that much energy anymore! I really try my best to just take things at a sensible pace these days. 

I certainly don't feel like I have a... a motor inside me, pushing me to keep moving all day. I actually quite enjoy sitting quietly in my favorite chair, even if my mind does wander off a bit. I hope it's alright to say that? I know some of the ladies my age at the center are involved in absolutely everything and never seem to stop moving, and I always feel a little guilty that I'm not quite so... industrious. But no, I wouldn't say I feel constantly on the go. 

I hope that's a helpful answer, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
